items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is short and matches Django's style. The make_msgid wrapper has a docstring ("Clean up make_msgid() to convert domain to idna ASCII."), the names say what they hold, and the try/encode('ascii') pattern is the one already used in sanitize_address.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same try/encode('ascii')/except/encode('idna') block is pasted into utils.get_fqdn and the new make_msgid, next to a third copy in sanitize_address, with no shared helper. Shadowing stdlib make_msgid as _make_msgid also changes the public django.core.mail.make_msgid, and makes the conversion run twice.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Only UnicodeEncodeError is caught, so the idna fallback runs only for non-ASCII names. IDNA failures are not swallowed and still surface. There are no magic constants and no resources to manage.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: CachedDnsName.get_fqdn converts at the source for every encoding, and ASCII hosts pass through unchanged. But the conversion is copied inline again in the make_msgid wrapper (redundant for DNS_NAME), instead of one shared helper.
